entries.author: assistant
entries.summary: P0-01 Postgres-in-prod — pool config in db.py + ADR-0020 recording the operational decision

changed: backend/app/db.py — Postgres branch gains pool_size=10, max_overflow=10, pool_pre_ping=True, pool_recycle=1800. SQLite branch unchanged (dev + hermetic tests keep today's behaviour). pool_pre_ping is load-bearing: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server reaps idle connections and without it the first request after an idle period 500s.

new_files: .context/decisions/0020-postgres-in-production.json — ADR-0020: production runs on Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server 16, same region as the app VM, SSL enforced, private endpoint, PITR 7d, dedicated non-superuser 'treasury_app' role. Connection string sourced from Key Vault (ties P0-06). Subsumes P3-03 (backup + snapshot) via the restore-drill invariant. Unblocks PHASE_2_MULTITENANCY_PLAN.md Stage 1 — RLS requires a real Postgres bind.
operational_followups: Provision the Flexible Server + 'treasury' DB + 'treasury_app' non-superuser role.
Put TREASURY_DATABASE_URL in Azure Key Vault; VM reads it at boot via managed identity (interim env-var acceptable, tracked as P0-06 debt).
Run alembic upgrade head against the new DB (CI already proves this is a no-op).
Perform the restore drill into a scratch DB and document the one-liner in scripts/. An untested backup is not a backup.

entries.author: assistant
entries.summary: S2 — planner settings + rate curve moved from in-process singletons to the tenant_setting table (restart-safe, per-tenant, scale-out ready)

changed: backend/app/models.py — new TenantSetting ORM class (id, tenant_id, key, payload_json, updated_at, updated_by_user_id; UNIQUE(tenant_id, key)); registered in PHASE_ONE_TABLES

backend/app/services/planner_settings.py — dropped module-level Lock + _settings singleton. get_settings/update_settings/reset_defaults now take (session, tenant_id). Defaults still live in the PlannerSettings dataclass; DB stores only the diff; a missing row returns defaults.

backend/app/services/system_policy.py — same shape for the rate curve. get_rate_curve/update_rate_curve/reset_rate_curve take (session, tenant_id). The 'DEFAULT_RATE_CURVE' table stays as the fallback.
backend/app/api/planner.py — three endpoints pass ctx.session + ctx.tenant_id through; writes commit explicitly; updated_by_user_id captured from the caller
backend/app/services/planner_service.py — _rate_for(session, tenant_id, rating, tenor); deploy_cash() passes self.session, self.tenant_id to get_settings and _rate_for
new_files: backend/app/repo/tenant_settings.py — thin repo with get, get_or_default, upsert, delete over the tenant_setting table
backend/alembic/versions/b17c3f04d2a8_tenant_setting_table.py — portable migration (no dialect-specific DDL)
new_tests: backend/tests/test_tenant_settings_persistence.py — 7 tests: planner settings survive a fresh session, are per-tenant, reset restores defaults, get-without-prior-write returns defaults; same three invariants for the rate curve

notes: Observable API shape is unchanged: GET /planner/settings returns the same JSON. Internals are per-tenant + persistent instead of per-process.

Behaviour change worth flagging: reset endpoints now DELETE the row instead of mutating a shared singleton. Next read returns dataclass defaults — same observable outcome. No code relied on singleton object identity.

Prerequisite for horizontal scaling: with the Postgres cutover (ADR-0020) + this change, two app instances now agree on what the planner settings are. Previously each instance held its own in-RAM copy.
Prerequisite for the parked multi-tenancy plan: every tenant now has its own planner knobs. One of the two in-memory places where tenant isolation was impossible is closed.
The tenant_setting table is a general per-tenant JSON-blob config store — future settings (e.g. accounting-event targets, hedge-advisor knobs) can land on it without another migration.

entries.author: assistant
entries.summary: S10 / P1-05 — composite index (tenant_id, occurred_at) on audit_event

changed: backend/app/models.py — AuditEvent.__table_args__ gains Index('ix_audit_tenant_occurred', 'tenant_id', 'occurred_at'). Every compliance query filters by tenant_id and orders/ranges on occurred_at; without this a scan of the table grew linearly with history.
new_files: backend/alembic/versions/c4f8e21a9b65_audit_event_tenant_occurred_index.py — portable migration (no dialect-specific DDL)

test_state.full_suite_after: phase0 model/migration parity green (58 passed); full suite unchanged

notes: Query shape surveyed in backend/app/api/compliance.py — 20+ sites filter by tenant_id and order/range on occurred_at. Composite covers all of them as a seek rather than a scan.

Deliberately not adding (tenant_id, action, occurred_at) or (tenant_id, subject_type, occurred_at) — the primary composite's selectivity on tenant_id alone is enough at today's row counts; add the three-column variant when a slow-query log justifies it.
Follow-up still open for P1-05 full close: nightly archive job for events > 7 years. Not shipped here; the index alone was the hot win.

entries.author: assistant
entries.summary: S1 — rate-limit store moved behind a port (Memory default, Redis adapter shipped)

changed: backend/app/connector/ports.py — new RateLimitStorePort Protocol: hit(key, max_requests, window_seconds) -> (allowed, retry_after); clear() for tests. Added to ALL_PORTS.

backend/app/connector/registry.py — _make_rate_limit_store() reads RATE_LIMIT_STORE env var (memory|redis). Redis path pulls REDIS_URL through SecretsPort (vault-uniform) and refuses to bind without it.

backend/app/services/rate_limit.py — rewritten to delegate to registry.get(RateLimitStorePort). Window arithmetic lives in the adapter now. Policy constants + FastAPI dependency surface unchanged — zero caller change.
new_files: backend/app/connector/adapters/rate_limit_store/__init__.py
backend/app/connector/adapters/rate_limit_store/memory.py — MemoryRateLimitStore: deque per key, thread-safe. Behaviour matches the previous in-module singleton exactly.

backend/app/connector/adapters/rate_limit_store/redis.py — RedisRateLimitStore: sorted-set sliding window via ZREMRANGEBYSCORE/ZCARD/ZADD/EXPIRE in a MULTI pipeline. redis-py is a lazy import; a deployment without it just leaves RATE_LIMIT_STORE=memory.

backend/tests/test_rate_limit_store.py — 9 tests covering the port contract (allowed-until-cap, cap refusal, key independence, window release, clear) + registry wiring (memory default, unknown refused, redis-without-url refused).

notes: No change in observable API behaviour. Every endpoint rate-limits exactly as before; the store is just pluggable.

Horizontal scaling unlock: set RATE_LIMIT_STORE=redis + REDIS_URL and N FastAPI instances share one bucket. Without this, each instance held its own in-RAM counter and the effective limit became N × policy.
Deliberately did NOT add Redis to backend/requirements.txt — it's an optional dep. A deployment that chooses redis adds `redis>=5` on its own. Tests use Memory only.
The clear() method is for tests; a prod Redis adapter wipes its namespace (scan+delete) and should never be called by application code.

entries.author: assistant
entries.summary: S9 — structured JSON logs with per-request context (request_id, tenant_id, user_id, path, method, status, duration_ms)

new_files: backend/app/logging.py — JsonFormatter + bind_request_context/clear_request_context/current_context on contextvars; configure() installs on the root logger. No third-party dep (stdlib logging + contextvars). get_logger() is the stable import surface so swapping in structlog later is one-line.
backend/app/middleware/__init__.py

backend/app/middleware/request_context.py — RequestContextMiddleware: reads or generates X-Request-Id, best-effort pulls user_id+tenant_id from the bearer token (same stateless read the rate limiter uses), binds everything into contextvars, logs request.start/request.end with method/path/status/duration_ms, echoes X-Request-Id on the response.

backend/tests/test_logging_context.py — 9 tests: formatter emits required keys, includes bound context, omits unbound keys, merges 'extra', coerces unserialisable; middleware echoes supplied X-Request-Id, generates one when missing, anon /health still succeeds.
changed: backend/app/main.py — app_logging.configure() at import; RequestContextMiddleware registered after CORS; CORS expose_headers gains X-Request-Id so a browser client can read the trace id.

notes: Every log line emitted during a request now carries the same request_id. Grep by request_id to see one request's trail across services; grep by tenant_id to see one tenant's.
Response header X-Request-Id is set on 2xx AND 5xx so an operator can correlate what the user saw with what the log shows.
Reserved stdlib LogRecord keys are filtered when merging 'extra' so a caller cannot overwrite 'ts' or 'level' by accident.
Unserialisable extra values are coerced via repr() rather than crashing the log call. Loud failure modes in logging land are the wrong trade.
uvicorn.access + sqlalchemy.engine.Engine quieted to WARNING in configure() — their default INFO torrent swamps the useful signal.
No existing log callsites were migrated. The infra is in place; a follow-up can route print()/console-mail/etc. through get_logger() when a specific debugging need demands it.

new_files: .gitignore (repo root) — ignores .project-memory/, .env, editor cruft. backend/.gitignore and frontend/.gitignore unchanged.
.claude/agents/solution-architect.md — planner/architect role, Read+Grep+Glob+Write+Edit only (deliberately NO Bash). Owns .context/decisions/ and PHASE_*.md. Never edits source files.

Reports done; does NOT tick the plan.

.claude/agents/frontend-engineer.md — Next.js 14 + TS + Tailwind, API-only data access, persona-pages behind role-nav (ADR-0009), compliance-tab shape (ADR-0016), X-Request-Id correlation to backend logs (S9). Reports done; does NOT tick the plan.

The whole Requirement→Research→Challenge→Plan→Isolate→Build→Review→Regression→Human testing→E2E→Scenario→Record Decisions flow. The three agents and their boundaries. Design constraints (reversibility, isolation, tenant isolation, additive-only, fail-closed authz). What the client gets vs raw prompts.
docs/prompts/kickoffs/.gitkeep — placeholder for per-feature kickoff prompts.

scripts/start-backend.ps1 — OneDrive-safe uvicorn --reload wrapper. Clears orphans on port 8000 + stale python processes under the project before launch. (Addresses the pytest-discovery hang we hit while running S1 tests today.)
scripts/start-frontend.ps1 — same shape for Next.js. Wipes .next with Remove-Item -Recurse -Force (OneDrive placeholders) before npm run dev.

.context/decisions/0021-feature-isolation-via-worktree.json — ADR-0021: D-03 'build features in a worktree against a DB copy, never the live dev DB'. Trivial changes exempt; worktree + copied TREASURY_DATABASE_URL for anything touching migrations or side-effectful services.

.context/decisions/0022-pcs-deferred.json — ADR-0022: PCS (Project Context System) is NOT installed. .context/changes/ + Claude Code auto-memory cover the memory need today. .project-memory/ pre-ignored for a future install.
changed: CLAUDE.md — new header block pointing at docs/AI_Assisted_Development_Framework.md, docs/MASTER_PROMPT_FEATURE_KICKOFF.md, .claude/agents/*, scripts/*, and naming the four standing rules (D-01..D-04).
deliberately_NOT_created: docs/DECISIONS.md — the Fusion template asks for a D-01 log but this project has 22 ADRs in .context/decisions/. Running the template verbatim would create a second decision log. User chose 'adapt, don't replace' explicitly.

docs/DELIVERY_PLAN.md — same reasoning; PHASE_2_BLUEPRINT.md + PHASE_2_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md + PHASE_2_ADMIN_UI_PLAN.md + PHASE_2_MULTITENANCY_PLAN.md are the plan tree. Parked plans are CI-enforced via PARKED_PLANS.json.

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md — .context/architecture.json + .context/data-model.json + .context/api.json + .context/backend.json + .context/frontend.json cover this richer, auto-regenerated by .context/update.py.
notes: Standing rules D-01 (additive) and D-04 (fail-closed authz) already matched the project's spirit — ADR-0018 (portable DDL + additive migrations), ADR-0011 (permission matrix), ADR-0013 (scope preflight), ADR-0015 (four-eye grants). The agent files now cite them directly so a new engineer agent inherits them.

D-02 reversibility (every migration has a tested downgrade): most existing migrations have a downgrade stub, but downgrade coverage isn't test-enforced today. Not addressed here — a follow-up could add an invariant test that asserts downgrade for every revision.
D-03 isolation (worktree per feature): new rule, formalised in ADR-0021. Not enforced by tooling yet — a `scripts/new-feature.sh` wrapper is the obvious follow-up.

PCS deferred (ADR-0022) because this project already has two memory layers (.context/changes/ + Claude Code auto-memory) that cover the same need. Revisit when a cross-session memory need surfaces that neither covers.
entries.next_step_for_user: First feature kickoff: copy docs/MASTER_PROMPT_FEATURE_KICKOFF.md, fill the Requirement block, paste into a fresh Claude Code session. The solution-architect agent returns a plan; nothing lands as code until that plan is reviewed.
